title: Negative (first pass at 20261026T0956-c37-q-lone-cell-peclet): raising the kernel drive mu to 2 or 4 does not make a lone C:swim-divide cell swim; transplanted cells grow 12-72x into crescent feeding fronts and split or tear within 15-335 t, travelling at most 1.8 diameters
summary: isolate_p.py (isolate.py from my audit 20261026T0618-c37-audit-kernelring, plus ISO_P overrides applied only after the growth phase, and a sample every 5 t so fast bodies are not lost). The claimed world (drive kernel, mu 1, kd 0.08, chi 5) grows from noise on seed 5 to t=2400. Then the 3 median cells are each copied alone into a fresh S=1 bath with mu=2 or mu=4 (vmax 1.0 so the drive does not clip) and followed until the first split, merge or loss. mu=2: cell 2 grows 72x into a crescent that moves 1.77 diameters (by mean area) and splits at t+335 (lone_mu2_view_cell2.png); cell 67 grows 24x and breaks up at t+45 after 0.77; cell 40 splits at once (it was dividing at transplant). mu=4: cells 2 and 67 grow 2.4x and 12x and break up within 20 t after 0.5-0.6 diameters. The same cells left in their crowd at the same mu move 0.7-2.9 diameters before a merge or split. At mu=1 (audit) lone cells grew 25-28x and split after <= 0.83. So a stronger drive does not cross a Michelin-type threshold here. In fresh substrate a lone cell's growth outruns its motion, and the body becomes a front. Untested: DS lower than 0.2, a fed bath held at the colony's depleted S, mu between 1 and 2.

finding.operator: label-free kernel substrate-gradient drive (v = mu G*(phi^2 grad S)/G*(phi^2)) on an isolated walled Allen-Cahn cell
finding.control: same cells left in their crowd at the same mu (in-place arm); mu=1 audit arm
finding.result: lone cells: mu 1 net <= 0.83 (area x25-28), mu 2 <= 1.77 (x24-72), mu 4 <= 0.56 (x2-12, torn within 20 t); none reaches 3 diameters
